judge_1.rationale: The second program is superior because it better fulfills the request for 'varied' sessions while maintaining the glute focus. It structures the three days with distinct upper-body emphases (Press, Row, Overhead), ensuring comprehensive upper-body development across the week. In contrast, the first program repeats the same upper-body exercises (Incline Press, Lat Pulldown) on Day 1 and Day 3, offering less variety. Additionally, the second program distributes the volume of the primary glute exercise (Machine Hip Thrust) more effectively by including it on all three days, whereas the first program omits it on Day 3, relying on a less effective isolation movement (Glute Kickback) instead. The second program's volume distribution for compound lifts is also more consistent.

judge_2.rationale: Both programs are 3-day full-body splits with glute emphasis (hip thrusts, hack squats, RDLs, glute bridges in warmups) and solid upper-body coverage. The second program distributes glute work more evenly across all three days (hip thrust on every day, plus hack squat and RDL on Day C), giving consistent glute attention throughout the week, while the first program's Day C is mostly upper-body with only glute kickbacks. The second also balances pressing/pulling better across days (press focus, row focus, overhead focus) and includes more variety (T-bar row, pullover). Both have sensible warmups and recovery; the second's arrangement is slightly more coherent and faithful to "extra attention to glutes while keeping upper-body work."

judge_1.rationale: The second program is superior because it adheres more faithfully to the 'front-side and back-side movement emphasis' request by creating distinct, focused sessions. It separates the primary lower body movements into a dedicated 'Front-Focus' (Quads) day and a 'Back-Focus' (Posterior Chain) day, allowing for higher quality and intensity on the primary lifts without the fatigue interference of mixing opposing movement patterns in the same session. In contrast, the first program attempts to combine heavy front-side and back-side lower body work on the same days (e.g., Day 1 has both Hack Squat and Hip Thrust), which dilutes the intensity of the primary movements and creates a less coherent split. Additionally, the second program's structure (Front/Back/Front/Back) provides better recovery management for the specific muscle groups compared to the first program's mixed approach.

judge_2.rationale: Both programs deliver 4 sessions alternating front-side/back-side emphasis with glute work (hip thrusts, kickbacks, glute bridges) in every session. The second program is more coherent: each day's content matches its label (Front-Focus = quads/chest/delts; Back-Focus = posterior chain/back), and glute volume is well distributed (thrusts on days 2-4, kickbacks on days 2 and 4). The first program's day 3 is labeled "Front-Side Upper & Glute Pump" yet leads with glute kickbacks/adduction, and its day 4 "Back-Side Pull & Glute Finisher" repeats hip thrust as the opener, making the front/back alternation less clean. The second also balances pressing/pulling and arm work more evenly across the week.

judge_1.rationale: The second program better fulfills the request to 'rotate movement emphasis' and 'leave recovery between hard lower-body days.' It explicitly structures the three days around distinct primary movements: Day A (Squat/Quad focus), Day B (Hinge/Hamstring focus), and Day C (Glute/Press focus). This ensures that the most taxing lower-body compound movements (Hack Squat, RDL, Hip Thrust) are separated by at least one day, allowing for better recovery. In contrast, the first program includes heavy leg isolation (Leg Extension) on Day 1, a heavy compound squat on Day 2, and a heavy hinge on Day 3. This results in consecutive days of significant lower-body stress (Day 1 and Day 2), which contradicts the user's specific request for recovery between hard lower-body days. The second program's naming convention and exercise selection also make the rotation of emphasis clearer and more logical.

judge_2.rationale: The second program more faithfully matches the request. Its three sessions are explicitly themed to rotate movement emphasis (A: squat/horizontal, B: hinge/vertical, C: glute/press), and each day leads with a distinct heavy lower-body pattern (hack squat, RDL, hip thrust) so hard lower-body days are separated by lighter or upper-body-focused work. The first program also rotates somewhat (press day, squat day, hinge day) but repeats many identical accessories across days, front-loads heavy lower-body work less clearly, and gives day 1 heavy leg curls/extensions plus day 2 heavy hack squat back-to-back with less differentiation. Both are 3-day full-body with similar volume, but the second's clearer rotation and better distribution of lower-body stress across the week make it the more coherent, balanced plan.
